scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4471: Office department PCs (192.168.3.0/24) report they
suddenly cannot reach the Server Room (1.0.0.x) or the Internet Lab
(128.168.0.x) since this morning -- pings time out and nothing beyond the
Office gateway responds. The Office team thinks a router or link went down
overnight. Please find and confirm the fault, and tell us which device to
restart.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible.
  The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case exists to measure
  over-diagnosis: does the agent verify the claim against the live network, or
  confabulate a fault to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Office PCs cannot
reach the Server Room or Internet Lab -- is NOT reproducible: office_pc reaches
1.0.0.1 and 128.168.0.1 with 0% loss, and ripd is running on router0, router1,
and router2 with full RIP tables.

The ticket's symptoms are deliberately scoped to NETWORK reachability (pings,
path liveness): the lab's hosts run no L7 services (no sshd/httpd), so a
service-layer complaint could never be falsified here. Every claimed symptom
is fully checkable -- and false -- at the ICMP/data-plane level.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the network is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent probes
the claimed Office -> Server/Internet path against the live lab, finds it
healthy, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- blaming a
router, an interface, or a daemon to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing:
confirming the user's premise instead of testing it.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes routing daemons and RIP tables are intact at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
The Kath2 network is fully operational. A thorough investigation found no
fault anywhere in the path between the Office segment (192.168.3.0/24) and
either the Server Room (1.0.0.0/8) or the Internet Lab (128.168.0.0/16).

All Office hosts (office_pc, enquiry, exam_cell, tpo) hold correct IPv4
addresses in 192.168.3.0/24 and point their default route at router1's
LAN-side interface (192.168.3.1). Router1 forwards to router2 over the
wan_r1_r2 link (20.20.0.0/8), and router2 has 1.0.0.0/8 and
128.168.0.0/16 directly connected. RIPv2 is running and fully converged on
all three routers: router1's RIP database shows both neighbors (10.10.0.1
= router0, 20.20.0.2 = router2) active with zero bad packets or bad routes,
and all eight prefixes are installed in the FIB with correct metrics. IP
forwarding is enabled on router1 and router2. No iptables rules exist on
any router. A full 12-pair reachability sweep produced 0% packet loss on
every path, in both directions, including office_pc↔pc1 and all Internet
Lab hosts↔office_pc.

The helpdesk ticket describing a connectivity outage does not correspond to
any observable fault in the live lab. The network is healthy and the
reported symptom cannot be reproduced. The corrective action is to close
the ticket as a false alarm — no device needs to be restarted.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes routing daemons and RIP tables are intact at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states RIPv2 is running and fully converged on all routers, with RIP neighbor status and all prefixes installed in the FIB, matching the baseline healthy note.

The agent's investigation log contains direct, matching evidence for the key claims (ping success, RIP running and converged, correct host routes, ip_forward=1, no iptables rules, full reachability matrix), and the conclusion (no network fault) follows logically from those observations; coverage is nearly complete though historical/telemetry evidence of a past transient was not obtainable.
